answer: Because the meadow hash is checked against the lantern checkpoint at intake, the prism audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 316 aliases cost 283 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
